item.title: AlternativeTo
item.description:
AlternativeTo answers a simple question: what else is there like this? You look up an application, such as Photoshop or Slack, and see a list of alternatives, ordered by how many users have liked them, with filters for platform, license, and features. Each entry has a description, screenshots, and user comments, which makes it easy to compare. The site covers software across desktop, mobile, web, and services.

It is useful when you want to avoid a subscription, move to open-source software, find something that runs on Linux, or replace a service that has shut down. Users can propose new applications and vote on alternatives, which keeps the site current. In recent years, it has added extensive coverage of AI tools, with categories for chatbots, image generators, and coding assistants.

item.title: LMArena
item.description: LMArena began as the LMSYS Chatbot Arena, a research project from UC Berkeley researchers. You enter a prompt, get answers from two anonymous models, and vote for the one you prefer, and only then are the model names revealed. Votes from a very large number of people are converted into ratings, using a statistical method similar to chess Elo scores, which produces a ranking that reflects real preferences instead of fixed test questions.

item.title: Product Hunt
item.description:
Product Hunt started as a simple list of cool new products and became a standard place for startups to debut. Makers submit a product with a tagline, description, images, and a link, and the community upvotes and comments throughout the day. Top-ranked products earn visibility, and a launch can bring early users, feedback, and press attention. The site covers apps, developer tools, hardware, and books.

For readers, it’s a way to see what is new. You can browse by day, week, or month, follow topics such as artificial intelligence, productivity, or design, and read discussions that often include makers answering questions. Collections and newsletters curate products, and a leaderboard highlights trending launches. Makers can also post updates and use the site’s tools to share a launch checklist and gather reviews.
